title: DARPA Selects Atom Computing, Diraq, IBM, and IonQ for Final Stage C Verification under Quantum Benchmarking Initiative - Quantum Computing Report
gist: DARPA selected Atom Computing, Diraq, IBM and IonQ for Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, the final physical-testing phase, joining Microsoft and PsiQuantum; agreements run up to $300M each for three of them and test utility-scale operation by 2033.

insights.claim: DARPA picked Atom Computing, Diraq, IBM and IonQ for Stage C of the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, shifting evaluation from R&D blueprint audits to direct physical testing and empirical validation of fault-tolerant architectures.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Stage C is the strongest public government validation filter in quantum hardware; selected firms gain credibility.
insights.locator: selected four commercial quantum hardware developers

insights.claim: The four join initial US2QC pilot participants Microsoft and PsiQuantum in Stage C, making six performers in total.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The cohort defines DARPA's shortlist across neutral atom, silicon spin, superconducting, trapped ion and others.

insights.claim: QBI launched in 2024 as an expansion of the US2QC program and tests whether platforms can reach utility-scale operation by 2033, defined as computational output value exceeding total capital and operating costs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The economic definition of utility scale is a stricter bar than qubit counts.
insights.locator: utility scale as the operational threshold

insights.claim: Stage C follows a yearlong Stage B that audited R&D execution plans, risk mitigation models and prototype data; DARPA's IV&V team will test under long-term agreements, managed by QBI Director Micah Stoutimore.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Independent verification of QPUs, control electronics, cryo packaging and decoders reduces reliance on vendor claims.

insights.claim: Atom Computing, Diraq and IonQ each have Stage C agreements with ceilings up to $300M; Diraq's has an initial $51M tranche and IonQ's runs through 2029.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Ceilings are not committed funds, but they signal potential federal revenue per company.

insights.claim: Atom Computing will be benchmarked on scaling across 1,200+ physical neutral-atom arrays in optical tweezers, with Microsoft providing algorithmic support and error-correction codes.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The Microsoft partnership ties a hyperscaler's QEC software to neutral-atom hardware.

insights.claim: Diraq plans to scale 300mm CMOS silicon spin-qubit chips from an 8-qubit data center deployment with Equinix in Sydney to 150,000 physical qubits by 2029 and over 2 million on a single die by 2031, supported by a $38 million CHIPS Act Letter of Intent.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Leveraging commercial foundry processes is the bull case for cost scaling; the 2031 target is aggressive.

insights.claim: DARPA will audit IBM's 2029 Starling architecture: modular superconducting transmons, meter-scale interconnects, multi-cell cryostats below 15 millikelvin and FPGA real-time QEC decoders in Qiskit; the matrix lists targets of 200 logical qubits and 100M gate operations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IBM's 2029 Starling is now subject to third-party verification.

insights.claim: IonQ will be tested on multi-generation Superion QPUs through 2029 (including Superion 256), 99.99% two-qubit fidelity, reconfigurable optical shuttling and simplified manufacturing economics.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Fidelity is established; the test is scaling and manufacturability.
